660	
661	Anything rsyncing into the Google Drive for Desktop mount (`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-*/`) needs `--modify-window=5`. Drive stores an mtime 1–2s below what rsync set, and for large files it stamps its own upload time instead (skew of hours). rsync's quick-check is size+mtime, so byte-identical files read as changed and are re-sent on **every** run, permanently.
662	
663	Diagnosed 2026-08-14 on `daily-backup.ps1` → `codex/sessions`: all 256 files size-identical, yet 134 re-sent nightly (252 MB). That perpetual write load into FUSE is what fed the wedge the watchdog was catching — the snapshot had been failing since 2026-08-06 (rsync exit 23, then 1, then 124 once the watchdog landed).
664	
665	**Why:** `du` on the mount reports less than the source (171M vs 289M) because Drive doesn't materialize every file — that discrepancy looks like an incomplete mirror and sends you hunting for missing data that isn't missing. Compare `stat -f%z` per file, not `du`.
666	
667	**How to apply:**
668	- Diagnose with dry runs, not `du`: `rsync -an -i <src>/ <dst>/ | grep -c '^>f'` with and without `--modify-window=5`. A large gap between the two *is* the diagnosis.
669	- Files already stamped with Drive's own upload time need a one-time `touch -r <src> <dst>`; the flag alone won't close a multi-hour skew. The repair sticks across Drive re-sync.
670	- Never substitute `--size-only` — `claude-projects` has genuine same-size edits that only mtime catches.
671	- Genuinely-new files re-send under both settings (gemini's 428 were all NEW). If the count is identical with and without the window, it's real work, not this bug.
672	
673	**`--modify-window` has a blind spot — cover it for SQLite (found 2026-08-15 while reviewing the fix).** The window makes rsync's quick-check tolerate a 5s mtime difference. That is safe for append-only logs, where any real change also moves the size. It is NOT safe for files rewritten in place at identical size — SQLite updates rows inside existing pages, so `~/.codex/sqlite/codex-dev.db` (229,376 B) can change content with size unchanged. If that write lands within 5s of the dest's Drive-rounded mtime, rsync skips it, and keeps skipping forever because neither side changes again.
674	
675	Reproduced: two 8-byte files, same size, content differing, mtimes 3s apart → `--modify-window=5` copies **0** files (silent loss); adding `--checksum` copies **1**. Fix in `daily-backup.ps1`: `Invoke-Rsync`/`Snapshot` take an `$extraArgs` param and the `.codex/sqlite` snapshot alone passes `--checksum`. Do not apply `--checksum` broadly — it re-reads every byte on both sides; it is cheap only because that DB is ~224 KB.
676	
677	**How to apply:** when adding a new `Snapshot` call, ask whether the source can change without changing size. Databases, fixed-width records, and image/binary formats with in-place headers all can — give those `--checksum`. Logs and transcripts cannot — leave them on the window.
678	
679	**One-way copy of new files into Drive: use `--ignore-existing`, never `--update` (2026-10-02).** `rsync -a --update` from `~/DEV/S2_Evaluation/data/` into the Drive mount hung 11 min, with nothing copied. `--update` did not skip files already on Drive, because Drive's mtimes are its own. The receiving child was blocked reading an existing Drive file. `--ignore-existing` copied the 2 missing files at once. macOS rsync is openrsync: its receiving child shows as `rsync --server`, so `pgrep -f "rsync -a ..."` misses it. Stop a hung run with TaskStop, not `kill`.

content.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Runs daily-backup.ps1 once at login, so a Mac that was off overnight still gets a backup.
# Skips if any daily-backup run already ended today (the nightly run or an earlier login run).
# shortcut: checks the log, not a lock file; two runs at the same moment could both start.
LOG="$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log"
TODAY=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
if grep -q "^$TODAY .*daily-backup end:" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null; then
  exit 0
fi
exec /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -s /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File "$HOME/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1"
----
{
 "id": "daily-backup",
 "label": "Daily memory + repo backup",
 "taskName": "KeystoneOS-DailyBackup",
 "exe": "pwsh",
 "script": "{USERPROFILE}/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1",
 "schedule": {
  "kind": "daily",
  "at": "21:00"
 },
 "graceMinutes": 60,
 "timeoutMinutes": 240,
 "maxAttemptsPerDay": 2,
 "reconcile": true,
 "makeupWindow": {
  "from": "21:00",
  "to": "23:59"
 },
 "successProbe": {
  "kind": "fileContains",
  "path": "{USERPROFILE}/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log",
  "pattern": "^{DATE} .*daily-backup end: OK"
 }
}

# RESTORE.md — Machine Recovery & Migration Guide

**For Eric.** If your machine crashed, was wiped, was returned to Baylor, or you're
setting up a new computer (Windows or Mac), this document walks you through getting
everything back. Written 2026-07-23 (system audit), maintained automatically.

## Where to find this document

You can read this from any device, no machine required:

1. **Canonical (always current):** https://github.com/erash11/dotclaude/blob/main/RESTORE.md
   — sign in to GitHub as **erash11**. Every edit is version-controlled; it cannot be
   silently corrupted, and the daily backup job pushes updates.
2. **Mirror:** Google Drive → `Backups/RESTORE.md` (drive.google.com, your gmail).
   Refreshed automatically every morning by the backup job.

Bookmark #1 on your phone. If you can reach either copy, you can recover everything.

## The map — where everything lives

| What | Primary home | Backup | Survives leaving Baylor? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Code & analysis projects (DEV) | this machine | GitHub `erash11/*` (private) | YES |
| SecondBrain vault (notes, meetings, insights) | `Desktop\SecondBrain` | GitHub `erash11/SecondBrain` | YES |
| Claude config, hooks, skills, agents, this file | `~\.claude` | GitHub `dotclaude`, `claude-skills` | YES |
| Claude working memory | `~\.claude\global-memory` | GitHub `claude-global-memory` | YES |
| Claude conversation history + project memories | `~\.claude\projects` | Google Drive `Backups/Machine/claude-projects` | YES |
| Codex memory, sessions, agents | `~\.codex` | Google Drive `Backups/Machine/codex` | YES |
| Gemini/Antigravity state | `~\.gemini` | Google Drive `Backups/Machine/gemini` | YES |
| Memory compiler + local patches | `~\.claude\claude-memory-compiler` | GitHub fork `erash11/claude-memory-compiler` | YES |
| Non-repo DEV work folders (Football, SpecialRequests, …) | `Desktop\DEV` | **SSD** `D:\AssistantBackup\DEV-nonrepo` + Baylor OneDrive | YES — SSD copy since 2026-08-03 |
| **Gitignored data inside git repos** (`forceplate.db`, `.rds`, outputs) | `Desktop\DEV\<repo>` | **SSD** `D:\AssistantBackup\DEV-repo-data` | YES — **was backed up NOWHERE before 2026-08-03** |
| **Uncommitted edits to tracked files** | `Desktop\DEV\<repo>` | **SSD** `D:\AssistantBackup\DEV-working-tree` | YES — added 2026-08-03 |
| Baylor work drive | Baylor OneDrive `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` | Baylor's problem | NO |

**Read the two bold rows above.** Pushing a repo backs up only its *tracked* files.
`ForcePlate_DecisionSystem` publishes 7 MB to GitHub against 1,709 MB on disk — the
database it runs on is gitignored. "All repos pushed clean" is true and says nothing about
whether your data survives. Coverage is declared in `~\.claude\scripts\backup-manifest.json`,
not inferred from whether a folder happens to be a git repo.

The personal/institutional split is recorded per path in that manifest as a `class` tag. As
of 2026-08-03 both classes are mirrored to the SSD by explicit decision; the tag exists so
institutional data stays identifiable and purgeable rather than blended in.

**Daily automation:** scheduled task `KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` (00:30) auto-commits and
pushes the memory repos, captures what git cannot carry to the SSD, snapshots the non-git
stores to the clouds above, and refreshes this document's Google Drive mirror. Each
destination gets a run-specific receipt read back after writing, so a run that copied
nothing cannot report success. The weekly stack doctor (Mondays) alarms if backups go
stale. Failures surface at the start of every Claude session.

**If the SSD is detached** the run warns (`backup-target-offline:SSD`) and continues —
your cloud backups still happen, but nothing gitignored is captured that night. Reattach
and the next run catches up.

## Accounts you need (before you start)

- **GitHub — erash11** (all code + config + notes). The keys to everything.
- **Google — your gmail** (Drive backups of transcripts/AI state).
- **Baylor Microsoft 365** (Baylor OneDrive — only if still employed).
- **Anthropic/Claude**, **OpenAI/Codex** (sign in on first launch).
- Re-auth on first use, they always rot: Fireflies, Google Drive/Gmail/Calendar MCP
  connectors, Supabase, Vercel, Catapult OpenField (token), VALD, Zotero.
- Passwords/2FA live in your password manager — **credentials are deliberately never
  in any backup** (`.credentials.json` and tokens are excluded everywhere).

## Scenario A — New Windows machine

Do these in order. Steps 1–3 get you functional; the rest completes the restore.

**1. Install the base tools**
Git (git-scm.com), GitHub CLI (`winget install GitHub.cli`), PowerShell 7
(`winget install Microsoft.PowerShell`), Node.js LTS, Claude Code, Codex CLI.
Python: use the **python.org installer** — NOT the Microsoft Store / Windows Install
Manager, which has silently deleted `C:\Python31x` during migrations twice and broken
everything downstream.
Sign in: OneDrive (Baylor account, if applicable) and **Google Drive for Desktop (gmail)**
— wait for Drive to mount as `G:`.

**2. Restore `~\.claude` — FIRST, before anything else**
```powershell
gh auth login          # erash11
cd $env:USERPROFILE\.claude
git init -b main
git remote add origin https://github.com/erash11/dotclaude.git
git fetch origin
git checkout -f origin/main -b main    # -f overwrites fresh-install defaults
git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-skills.git        $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\skills
git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-global-memory.git $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\global-memory
git clone https://github.com/erash11/claude-memory-compiler.git $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\claude-memory-compiler
```
This brings back your settings, hooks, agents, all skills, working memory, and the
backup script itself.

**3. Restore conversation history and AI state from Google Drive**
```powershell
robocopy "G:\My Drive\Backups\Machine\claude-projects" "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\projects" /E
robocopy "G:\My Drive\Backups\Machine\codex"           "$env:USERPROFILE\.codex" /E
robocopy "G:\My Drive\Backups\Machine\gemini"          "$env:USERPROFILE\.gemini" /E
```

**4. Restore work**
```powershell
mkdir $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\DEV; cd $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\DEV
gh repo list erash11 --limit 100      # your full inventory — clone what you need
git clone https://github.com/erash11/KeystoneOS.git
git clone https://github.com/erash11/SecondBrain.git $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\SecondBrain
git clone https://github.com/erash11/morning-briefing.git   # RETIRED 2026-08-14 - restore only if reviving
```
> `morning-briefing` was retired 2026-08-14 (job disabled, project removed from disk, dropped from
> the backup manifest). Skip it on a restore unless you are deliberately reviving it. Its output —
> 56 briefings — lives in `SecondBrain/morning-briefings/` and is restored with the vault.
Non-repo folders (if still at Baylor): copy back from Baylor OneDrive `Backups\DEV-NonRepo`.

**5. Rebuild Python environments**
```powershell
cd $env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\DEV\morning-briefing
python -m venv .venv; .venv\Scripts\pip install -r requirements.txt
cd $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\claude-memory-compiler   # uses uv — see its README
pip install memsearch
```
**CRITICAL:** after any `pip install` of memsearch, re-apply the local flush patch
(notes in the compiler repo). Symptom when missing: errors in
`global-memory\transcripts\.errors.log` every session.
Milvus (memsearch's vector DB): start per `~\.memsearch\config.toml` (localhost:19530),
then reindex. The index is rebuildable — nothing is lost if it's gone.

**6. Re-register the scheduled tasks**
```powershell
$pwsh = 'C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe'; $U = $env:USERPROFILE
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS Morning'     -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $pwsh -Argument "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -File `"$U\Desktop\DEV\KeystoneOS\scripts\morning-cadence.ps1`"") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 06:00) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS-DailyBackup' -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $pwsh -Argument "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -File `"$U\.claude\scripts\daily-backup.ps1`"") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 06:15) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS-StackDoctor' -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $pwsh -Argument "-NoProfile -File `"$U\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\weekly-check.ps1`"") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Weekly -DaysOfWeek Monday -At 06:40) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'MorningBriefing'        -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "$U\Desktop\DEV\morning-briefing\scripts\run_with_logging.cmd") -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At 07:20) -Settings (New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -StartWhenAvailable)
# KeystoneOS-AgySync: see KeystoneOS\scripts\keystone.ps1 (agy-sync, Windows PowerShell 5)
```

**7. Verify**
```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\stack-check.ps1"
```
`ALL CLEAR` = you're fully back. Or just open Claude Code and say "run stack doctor".

## Scenario B — Moving to a Mac

Everything cloud-side is platform-neutral (GitHub + Google Drive). The translation:

| Windows | Mac |
|---|---|
| `C:\Users\eric_rash\` | `/Users/eric_rash/` (`~`) |
| winget installs | Homebrew: `brew install git gh node powershell` + python.org installer |
| PowerShell 7 | Works on Mac (`pwsh`) — but the backup script uses robocopy; see below |
| robocopy | `rsync -a --delete` |
| Task Scheduler | `launchd` or `cron` (`crontab -e`: `15 6 * * * /path/to/backup.sh`) |
| `G:\My Drive` | `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-<gmail>/My Drive` |
| Baylor OneDrive | `~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-BaylorUniversity` |

**For a planned move to a Mac, follow `MIGRATION-MACOS.md` instead of this section.** It
is the ordered, executable procedure with pinned versions, the `DEV-repo-data` overlay
step, credential inventory, and launchd conversions. This section remains only as the
emergency summary.

Steps: same order as Scenario A — tools, `~/.claude` from the dotclaude repo, snapshots
from Google Drive or the SSD, repos from GitHub, venvs, then scheduling. The one real port
is `daily-backup.ps1` (robocopy + Register-ScheduledTask are Windows-only).

**Correction (2026-08-03):** an earlier version of this document claimed
`~\.claude\settings.json` and the hooks hardcode `C:\Users\eric_rash`. They do not. An
audit found exactly three files that do: `CLAUDE.md`, `scripts\daily-backup.ps1`, and
`scripts\fix-msys-ad-stall.ps1`. The port is smaller than this document used to imply.

**Also note:** the SSD is NTFS and macOS mounts it read-only. You can restore *from* it but
cannot back up *to* it until you reformat to exFAT. See `MIGRATION-MACOS.md` Step 10 — this
will silently break your nightly backup on the new machine if missed.

## Deliberately NOT backed up

- `~\.codex\work` (19+ GB of disposable working clones)
- Milvus / memsearch index (rebuilt by reindexing)
- Caches, tool binaries, `.venv` folders (rebuilt by installers)
- **All credentials** — `.credentials.json`, OAuth tokens, API keys. By design.
  They live in your password manager and re-auth flows.
- `D:\ CRASHBOX` legacy backup drive — historical, not part of this system.

## Keeping this document honest

The daily backup job pushes this file to GitHub and mirrors it to Google Drive on every
run. When the system changes (new scheduled task, new repo, new store), whoever makes the
change — usually Claude — must update this file in the same session. If you read this and
it contradicts reality, run the stack doctor and ask Claude to reconcile RESTORE.md.

#!/bin/bash
# restore.command — mechanical restore for the MacBook (Phases 0–5).
# Written 2026-08-04 on the old Windows machine. NEVER EXECUTED ON macOS.
# Treat the first run as a test. Dry-run is the default for that reason.
#
# Covers: drive check, base tools, ~/.claude, AI state, ALL DEV projects
#         (clone + the gitignored-data overlay + non-repo folders), venvs.
# Does NOT cover: credentials, launchd, porting the backup script, skill triage.
#         Those need judgment or your input — open Claude Code and use START-HERE.md
#         Phases 6–9. This script tells you that when it finishes.
#
# Usage:
#   double-click in Finder      -> dry run, changes nothing
#   ./restore.command --run     -> actually do it
#
# Safety rules baked in: never deletes anything, never writes to the backup drive,
# skips work already done (safe to re-run after a failure), stops on first error.

set -uo pipefail

MODE="dry"
[ "${1:-}" = "--run" ] && MODE="run"

RED=$'\033[31m'; GRN=$'\033[32m'; YLW=$'\033[33m'; BLD=$'\033[1m'; RST=$'\033[0m'
LOG="$HOME/restore-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log"
FAILED=0

say()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }
ok()   { printf '  %sOK%s   %s\n' "$GRN" "$RST" "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }
warn() { printf '  %sWARN%s %s\n' "$YLW" "$RST" "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }
bad()  { printf '  %sFAIL%s %s\n' "$RED" "$RST" "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; FAILED=$((FAILED+1)); }
hdr()  { printf '\n%s=== %s ===%s\n' "$BLD" "$*" "$RST" | tee -a "$LOG"; }

# run CMD... — executes unless dry mode
run() {
  if [ "$MODE" = "dry" ]; then printf '  would run: %s\n' "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; return 0; fi
  "$@" >>"$LOG" 2>&1
}

say "${BLD}Restore — Phases 0–5${RST}"
say "mode: $MODE      log: $LOG"
[ "$MODE" = "dry" ] && say "${YLW}DRY RUN — nothing will change. Re-run with --run to execute.${RST}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Phase 0

findings.title: Snapshot-Gws ignores tar's exit code, so a partial archive is uploaded and logged OK
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1:290 `& /usr/bin/tar @tarArgs 2>$null` followed only by `if (-not (Test-Path "$tmpDir/$archiveName"))` (291). $LASTEXITCODE is never checked. The upload then overwrites the single Drive copy in place via `drive files update` (306-308).
findings.impact: A tar that fails partway (unreadable file, file changed during read) still produces an archive. It replaces the last good Drive snapshot with no error, and only Drive's own revision history (not checked) could bring it back.
findings.fix: After tar, `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { $Errors.Add(...); Log ...; return }`. Optionally run `tar -tzf` before upload, and keep yesterday's copy (rename it before update) so a bad archive cannot replace the only good one.

findings.title: Snapshot-Gws ignores tar's exit code, so a partial archive is uploaded and logged OK

findings.impact: A tar that fails partway (unreadable file, file changed during read) still produces an archive. It replaces the last good Drive snapshot with no error, and only Drive's own revision history (not checked) could bring it back.
findings.fix: After tar, `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { $Errors.Add(...); Log ...; return }`. Optionally run `tar -tzf` before upload, and keep yesterday's copy (rename it before update) so a bad archive cannot replace the only good one.

findings.title: Scheduled 21:00 nightly backup has not completed OK since 2026-10-13; it runs while the Mac sleeps on battery
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log run end lines: 10-14 01:50 run ERROR(1); 10-14 21:10 -> 10-15 06:32 ERROR(7); 10-15 22:11 -> 10-16 06:01 ERROR(7); 10-17 21:09 -> 10-19 06:25 ERROR(7) (33 h, memsearch INDEX 10-18 01:47 -> 10-19 05:36); 10-19 21:00 run has NO end line (last line 10-20 00:05:30 'INDEX path set'); 10-20 21:06 -> 10-21 09:26 ERROR(7); 10-21 21:03 -> 10-22 06:05:12 ERROR(5). Last scheduled OK: 10-13 06:00:02. All OK runs since then (10-14 10:52, 10-19 17:28, 10-22 06:53) were daytime runs not started by launchd. `launchctl print gui/501/com.keystone.dailybackup`: runs = 2, last exit code = 1. That is daily-backup.ps1:751 `if ($Errors.Count -gt 0) { exit 1 }` on the 10-21 run's 5 errors: repo-diverged:global-memory plus snapshot claude-projects/codex-sessions/gemini/launchagents .tgz (gws 'Connection reset' 500s and 401 'Drive auth failed: Failed to get token'). `pmset -g log`: 10-21 20:32-21:42 repeated 'DarkWake from Deep Idle ... Using BATT (Charge:26%)' / 'Maintenance Sleep'; 18 DarkWakes 02:00-06:59; the first full 'Wake from Deep Idle ... lid' was 10-22 05:46:28 (and 10-21 09:21:18, 5 minutes before that run ended). The plist runs `/usr/bin/caffeinate -i -s pwsh ...`. `man caffeinate`: '-s ... This assertion is valid only when system is running on AC power.' The 10-17 and 10-19 nightly pushes failed with 'Could not resolve host: github.com'.
findings.impact: The Drive .tgz layer (Tier A memory, transcripts, Codex/Gemini state, LaunchAgents, live DBs) only lands on mornings Eric opens the lid while the run is still going, or when someone runs it by hand. On 10-20 every Drive upload failed and the run never finished. Each nightly run holds pwsh for 9-33 hours.
findings.fix: Run the backup when the Mac is awake and on AC, not at 21:00 with the lid shut. Options: move StartCalendarInterval to a daytime desk hour, or add a wake/AC trigger (a wrapper that exits unless `pmset -g ps` shows AC and the network is reachable, re-fired by a short StartInterval until it succeeds once that day). Do not rely on caffeinate -s on battery. Also update STORAGE.md Known gaps, which still says '00:30'.
findings.known_where: Partly. ~/.claude/STORAGE.md Known gaps line 76 ('nightly 00:30 gws uploads fail when the Mac is offline or asleep') and ~/DEV/docs/STATUS.md 2026-10-20 entry record single-night failures. findings.evidence: ~/.claude/RESTORE.md (mtime 2026-08-14, 191 lines): Scenario A is Windows; restores AI state with `robocopy "G:\My Drive\Backups\Machine\claude-projects"`, but backups are now .tgz archives in _MACHINE/Backups/Machine (daily-backup.ps1:466-475) and have to be fetched with gws. It also says 'KeystoneOS-DailyBackup (00:30)', Milvus, a bare `pip install memsearch` (PEP 668), and a morning-briefing venv. It does not mention dev-databases.tgz, Cloud_Copy or CRASHBOX on the Mac. ~/.claude/restore.command (mode -rw-r--r--, not executable): header says 'NEVER EXECUTED ON macOS'. Phase 0 requires $SSD/repos and $SSD/MANIFEST and exits 1 on 'MISSING'. Memory documents the CRASHBOX roots as DEV-nonrepo, DEV-repo-data, DEV-working-tree, claude, codex, gemini, SecondBrain and _receipts (no repos/MANIFEST). It sets DEV="$HOME/Desktop/DEV" (actual ~/DEV) and hardcodes 16 repos, including DexaProject (which has no repo) and morning-briefing (retired), against 128 DEV manifest entries. It defers to ~/.claude/MIGRATION-MACOS.md (mtime 08-14) and START-HERE.md (09-07). The nightly still uploads this RESTORE.md to Drive ('RESTORE.md mirrored to _MACHINE/Backups/ (via gws)').
findings.impact: In a crash, the guide Eric is told to bookmark points to wrong paths and formats, and the script aborts at Phase 0. Recovery would have to be worked out under pressure.
findings.fix: Rewrite RESTORE.md for the Mac: gws download of each _MACHINE/Backups/Machine/*.tgz then tar -xzf; dev-databases.tgz; repos from `gh repo list`; CRASHBOX layout; the launchd plists in launchagents.tgz. Either update restore.command to the current SSD layout and ~/DEV, or retire it. Then test it on a scratch user or folder.

findings.title: Nightly SSD layer reads DexaProject through the Drive FUSE mount and copies identifiable health data to the exFAT CRASHBOX
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json line 1465: path 'Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/DexaProject', destinations ['ssd']. daily-backup.log 2026-10-22 06:19:02 'STATE-SSD Library/CloudStorage/.../DexaProject -> DexaProject : OK' (rsync via Snapshot-Additive, daily-backup.ps1:588-606). Manifest destinations.ssd says filesystem exFAT. CREDENTIALS.md has an 'Accepted exception — credential files on the transport drive' section.
findings.impact: An rsync read through the mount can hang (memory project_drive-fuse-read-hang.md: default is gws, never the mount); it is bounded only by the 900 s rsync watchdog. Identifiable health data and credential files sit on a portable drive that macOS cannot encrypt natively as exFAT.
findings.fix: Confirm whether CRASHBOX is encrypted at the hardware level. If not, move to an APFS-encrypted volume or drop DexaProject from the SSD layer. If the copy stays, fetch it with gws instead of rsync through the mount.
findings.known_where: The manifest entry is deliberate (memory notes DexaProject 'declared'). The mount-read risk and the encryption question are not recorded.

findings.title: Snapshot-Gws ignores tar's exit code, so a partial archive is uploaded and logged OK
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1:290 `& /usr/bin/tar @tarArgs 2>$null` followed only by `if (-not (Test-Path "$tmpDir/$archiveName"))` (291). $LASTEXITCODE is never checked. The upload then overwrites the single Drive copy in place via `drive files update` (306-308).
findings.impact: A tar that fails partway (unreadable file, file changed during read) still produces an archive. It replaces the last good Drive snapshot with no error, and only Drive's own revision history (not checked) could bring it back.
findings.fix: After tar, `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { $Errors.Add(...); Log ...; return }`. Optionally run `tar -tzf` before upload, and keep yesterday's copy (rename it before update) so a bad archive cannot replace the only good one.
